newsitem.title: CANADA: WCE canola ends down on commercial, fund selling.
newsitem.headline: WCE canola ends down on commercial, fund selling.

text.p: WCE canola futures ended down on commercial and fund selling, traders said.

"Cargill sold a few hundred November, funds sold 500 November, there were hedges at the close. There's talk of European seed coming to Eastern Canada because we're $25 overpriced," a trader said. November WCE canola crush profit margins rose to -6.95 Friday from -10.14 Thursday. Sep-Nov spread at $2. Volume was 2,350 lots, or 47,000 tonnes.
August canola fell $4.80 to $358.20, November down $4.70 to $339.20. September flax rose $3.70 to $290.60 on talk of a shortage of stocks for export, November up $1.50 to $281.
Sep-Nov flax spread from $7 to $9. Volume was 835 lots.

October western barley lost $0.80 to $125.70, December down $1 to $126.90 on the Canadian Wheat Board's C$5 a tonne cut in its estimate of world feed barley values Thursday and lower CBOT corn. Volume was 300 lots.

October feed wheat lost $2.70 to $150.10 on commercial selling, December down $2.30 to $150.50 on the CWB's C$6 to C$9 reduction in its world wheat price outlook. About 200 Mar May spread at $1. Volume was 745 lots.
LFG bought October feed peas unchanged at US$170 from UGG while 60 Oct-Dec was spread at US$0.40.
March oats fell US$1.50 to set a new low of US$116.50 as Pioneer bought from Louis Dreyfus. Volume was 20 lots.
(All values in Canadian dollars except oats, feed peas).
